Per-experiment average (5.0 min) is a new project best (vs .60's 5.52 min), confirming the regression is driven entirely by experiment count growth (+17 experiments) and full-milestone carry contamination, not per-experiment inefficiency.
headline_finding: FULL-MILESTONE WALL TIME REGRESSION: +32 min (+0.9%) vs .60 (3656 min), +273 min (+8.0%) vs .58 baseline (3415 min). UNPRECEDENTED BOTTLENECK FREEZE: All five slowest experiments are IDENTICAL to .60 slowest-5 (Exp 786, 527, 491, 627, 603) — the first time in project history that zero composition change occurred in the full-milestone slowest-5 across two consecutive milestones. The per-experiment average (5.0 min) is the new project best, confirming individual-experiment efficiency is NOT the problem. The problem is the documented-but-unapplied recommendation loop: the same 9 improvement actions were written in the .60 retro and not applied before .61 execution began. CONDUCTOR CYCLE ACHIEVED 9.4 MIN TOTAL for 12 experiments — a structural breakthrough that demonstrates the managed roadmap approach works. The full-milestone overhead is 3679 min of non-conductor carry (99.7% of total wall time comes from historical unguarded queue sources). GPU close: CLEAN (4MB/0%/48C and 4MB/0%/38C, 10C thermal differential — GPU 1 underutilized, widening from .60's 8C gap). CPMI WIRING MISS: Exp 798 generated augmentation_ratio=2.5 CPMI pairs; Exp 799 trained with augmentation_ratio=1.0. JEPA v21 ood_auc=0.2444 is an all-time low caused by a wiring disconnect, not an algorithmic failure.

slowest_experiments.title: Gemma4 OOM Fix v3 + VR Threshold Grid (GPU REQUIRED)
slowest_experiments.root_cause: RETRO-028 fourth+ consecutive milestone without closure. Exp 786 ran the .60 milestone's Fix v3 grid; Exp 795 (.61) achieved only partial_success for Fix v4. The full-milestone slowest-5 still shows Exp 786 from the historical queue (the .61 cycle's Exp 795 is not yet in the slowest-5 because its duration was sub-threshold in the managed cycle). Gemma4-E4B-it requires ~14.89 GiB VRAM; concurrent resident processes push OOM. The three-step isolation protocol (kill_gpu_zombies + pkill VRAM holders + nvidia-smi verify before load) has not been fully applied across all four fix attempts. Each failed attempt without checkpoint save produces zero partial artifacts despite 60-90 min wall time. Resolution path: Fix v5 must add nvidia-smi loop verification at each isolation step with an abort-and-report if VRAM does not clear within 30s. Use GPU 1 (38C, cooler by 10C) as Gemma4 target.

slowest_experiments.title: Live 100q Precision v8 — RETRO-033 eighth attempt
slowest_experiments.root_cause: RETRO-033 was definitively closed in .57 (Exp 742, seed=999 +0.00510). Manifest enforcement confirmed for conductor cycle in .58 (Exp 754). Exp 527 continues to re-execute from unguarded historical queue sources for the eighth consecutive post-retirement milestone. Cumulative post-retirement waste: ~416 min across 8+ appearances. The manifest_fix_patch.txt covers only the conductor-managed dequeue path. The full-milestone presence of Exp 527 (.58, .59, .60, .61 — 4 documented full-milestone appearances) proves that at minimum 3 additional dequeue call sites bypass the manifest. Each dequeue site must implement the same exclusion check. This is not a research or algorithmic problem — it is a single code fix in scripts/research_conductor.py.

slowest_experiments.title: JEPA Curriculum Diagnostic — why did quality-gate cause regression
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Third consecutive .58+.60+.61 slowest-5 appearance. Diagnostic experiment performing a full JEPA training loop to investigate quality-gate regression. The 52 min runtime indicates unbounded execution — the diagnostic would produce actionable signal (loss plateau identification, epoch-level AUC) within the first 3-4 training epochs (~10-15 min). Adding ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog at 20 min with checkpoint save per epoch would preserve partial results and exit cleanly. The JEPA OOD regression root cause (quality-gate interaction) has been identified from other angles (Exp 693, .53) — this diagnostic may already be obsolete. Retirement candidate if JEPA v21 root cause (CPMI wiring miss) explains the regression trajectory.

slowest_experiments.title: interwhen Mid-Generation Monitor — SymCodeVerifier at mid-generation
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Third consecutive .58+.60+.61 slowest-5 appearance. Architecture: sentence-by-sentence text generation with SymCodeVerifier called after each sentence. For 100q at ~0.3s/verification × N sentences/answer, overhead multiplies with generation depth. The paragraph-boundary batching fix (every 3-4 sentences) was recommended in .58 retro, documented in .60 retro, and still not implemented. This is now the third consecutive milestone where the same optimization is described but not applied. A 2-hour implementation would reduce this from 51 min to ~15 min per 100q run. The recommendation has been carried forward three consecutive milestones; if it is not implemented in .62 Phase 0, it should be escalated to a RETRO-class item with a mandatory gate.

slowest_experiments.title: CoACEExtractorV4 — Data-Driven Live Training via GenPRM
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Third consecutive .58+.60+.61 slowest-5 appearance. Productive research — GenPRM-based live extractor training requires a full GPU training run. Exp 603 is NOT a retirement candidate (it produces value). It IS a DualGPU migration candidate: training on GPU 1 (38C, 10C cooler, underutilized) while inference runs on GPU 0 via ThreadPoolExecutor yields 1.8319x speedup (validated Exp 746, .57). Applying DualGPU reduces from 44 min to ~24 min. This migration was recommended in .58 retro, documented in .60 retro, and not applied for the third consecutive milestone. Same documentation-without-application pattern as Exp 627. Both migrations are 2-4 hour implementations with validated speedup factors.

bottlenecks_identified: UNPRECEDENTED COMPOSITION FREEZE — ALL 5 SLOWEST IDENTICAL ACROSS TWO CONSECUTIVE MILESTONES: This is the first time in project history that zero composition change occurred in the full-milestone slowest-5 between consecutive milestones (.60 and .61 have the identical top 5). The five experiments (786, 527, 491, 627, 603) have persisted for 2-3 consecutive milestones each. This is not a coincidence or bad luck — it is structural evidence that the action loop is broken: retrospective recommendations are being written, documented, and then not applied before the next milestone begins. The bottleneck is in the recommendation-to-implementation pipeline, not in the experiments themselves.

DOCUMENTATION-WITHOUT-APPLICATION LOOP (NOW IN 3rd CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE): Nine improvement actions were documented in the .60 retro (manifest enforcement, timeout governance, DualGPU migration, paragraph batching, Gemma4 isolation, CPMI wiring, experiment count governance, thermal routing, recommendation closure tracking). None were applied before .61 execution began. The .57 retro also documented the same core actions. Three consecutive full milestones with the same documented-but-unapplied improvements confirm that the current retrospective process generates zero operational change. Retrospective writing is now the highest-cost low-value activity in the pipeline.

EXP 527 UNGUARDED QUEUE — 8th+ POST-RETIREMENT APPEARANCE: Exp 527 was retired in .57, excluded from the conductor cycle since .58 (manifest enforcement confirmed). It continues to run from historical queues in full-milestone timing for .58, .59, .60, and .61 — four consecutive documented appearances post-retirement. The manifest_fix_patch.txt covers only the conductor managed dequeue path. At minimum 3 other dequeue call sites exist and bypass the manifest. Cumulative waste since retirement: ~416 min. This is a single code fix requiring 30-60 minutes of engineering time — with a 416 min payback already accrued.

SEQUENTIAL GPU USE WITH WIDENING THERMAL DIFFERENTIAL: GPU 1 close temperature dropped from 44C (.60) to 38C (.61) while GPU 0 held at 48C. The 10C gap (widened from .60's 8C) confirms GPU 1 ran even less compute relative to GPU 0 in .61. Both GPUs idle at close with 4MB driver-level allocations. DualGPU validated at 1.8319x speedup (Exp 746, .57) but training-heavy experiments (Exp 603, Exp 786 grid, JEPA diagnostics) all ran sequentially on GPU 0. The thermal evidence shows a widening, not narrowing, utilization asymmetry — DualGPU migration is moving further from implementation, not closer.

RETRO-028 FOURTH CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE WITHOUT CLOSURE: Exp 786 (Fix v3, .60), Exp 795 (Fix v4, .61, partial_success). Each closure attempt runs 60-90 min without verified checkpoint-save-per-grid-row. The four-step isolation protocol has been described three times but never fully verified via nvidia-smi loop. Without a strict nvidia-smi verification gate (VRAM < 500MB before load), each attempt may start with residual allocation that triggers OOM mid-grid. The partial_success in Exp 795 represents progress but is insufficient to unblock Exp 796 (SOTA GGUF code repair, still gated).

CPMI-TO-TRAINING WIRING MISS (NEW — JEPA v21 ALL-TIME LOW): Exp 798 generated CPMI pairs with augmentation_ratio=2.5. Exp 799 (JEPA v21 retrain) ran with augmentation_ratio=1.0 — the CPMI corpus was not passed as the training data argument. JEPA v21 ood_auc=0.2444 is the lowest in project history (below random 0.5). The CPMI algorithmic contribution cannot be evaluated because the experiment ran without it. This is an implementation handoff error, not an algorithmic failure. A pre-run assertion (assert augmentation_ratio > 1.0) would have caught this at script startup before any training began.

SYNTHETIC INFERENCE STUB BLOCKING CONSTRAINT EVALUATION: Exps 801 and 802 both show zero delta (constraint_addition_delta=0.0) because the inference mode is a deterministic synthetic_cpu placeholder. The EmbeddingConstraintStore retrieval is correct (AUC=0.92). The constraint signal is not reaching the energy function — the connection between retrieval and IsingEBM.infer() is a stub. All constraint addition experiments since RETRO-CONSTRAINT-ZERO-DELTA opened have evaluated a placeholder, not the real inference path. The fix requires wiring EmbeddingConstraintStore output into IsingEBM.infer() as soft penalty inputs on the spin coupling matrix.

FPGA TOOLCHAIN THIRD CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE BLOCKED: KV260 board arrived 2026-04-20. Exps 791 (.60), 794 (.61), and 804 (.61) all failed at tool-check stage (yosys=False, nextpnr_ice40=False, icepack=False). The fix is a single pacman command (pacman -S yosys nextpnr icestorm) that takes 5-10 minutes. Three milestone cycles of blocked KV260 experiments represent a recurring avoidable bottleneck.

EXPERIMENT COUNT GROWTH AS STRUCTURAL REGRESSION DRIVER: 679 experiments in .61 vs 662 in .60 (+17). At 5.0 min/experiment average, 17 new experiments contribute ~85 min of additional wall time. Without structural interventions (retirement from all queues, experiment count cap), continued growth guarantees wall-time regression regardless of per-experiment efficiency improvements. The per-experiment average has improved monotonically (7.4 min in .52 → 5.0 min in .61), but this efficiency gain is structurally outpaced by experiment accumulation.

A one-page checklist file (MILESTONE_PREREQS.md) listing all IMMEDIATE-class retro actions from the prior retro must be checked and signed off before any milestone experiment runs. Wiring the constraint feature vector into IsingEBM's spin coupling matrix is the single fix that simultaneously resolves RETRO-CONSTRAINT-ZERO-DELTA and RETRO-TIER1-PLATEAU. DualGPU validated at 1.8319x speedup (Exp 746, .57). GPU 1 at 38C with 0% utilization has maximal thermal headroom. Estimated savings: 20 min/Exp 603 run, 25 min/JEPA-diagnostic run. Recommended in .58 retro, documented in .60 retro, third consecutive milestone without implementation.

PROCESS — Enforce experiment count cap at 700 cumulative with mandatory retirement sweep before new experiments queue: The project has grown from 538 experiments (.52) to 679 (.61) in 9 milestone cycles (+15 experiments/milestone average). At 5.0 min/experiment, each new experiment permanently adds 5 min to every subsequent milestone. Retiring completed experiments from ALL queue sources before adding new ones is the only sustainable path. Recommend cap at 700 with retirement-sweep as Phase 0 prerequisite in every milestone from .62 forward.
